claim: FBI IC3 reported approximately USD 55.5 billion in exposed BEC losses between October 2013 and December 2023 and described continued use of payment processors and cryptocurrency services
source_title: Business Email Compromise: The $55 Billion Scam
notes: Global exposed-loss figure; not limited to financial-sector victims

claim: Coinbase reported that criminals bribed and recruited rogue overseas support agents who abused access to customer-support systems and stole data used for later social engineering
source_title: Protecting Our Customers - Standing Up to Extortionists
notes: Company-provided facts; full criminal structure and all affected individuals are not public

claim: FS-ISAC and Akamai reported that financial services were the top target for volumetric DDoS attacks in 2024 and described increasingly precise attacks
source_title: From Nuisance to Strategic Threat: DDoS Attacks Against the Financial Sector
notes: Supports availability and operational-resilience analysis

claim: ENISA reported that DDoS represented 77 percent of recorded incidents in its 2025 EU threat landscape and that finance represented 4.5 percent of targeted sectors
source_title: EU consistently targeted by diverse yet convergent threat groups
notes: High incident volume did not always produce high disruption; useful for separating frequency from impact

claim: FS-ISAC identified fraud and scams using generative AI, supplier attacks, geopolitical uncertainty, DDoS and ransomware as key risks in its 2025 review
source_title: Heightened Cyber Threats are Testing the Operational Resilience of the Financial Sector
notes: Report draws on member institutions across 75 countries

claim: The EU Digital Operational Resilience Act has applied since 17 January 2025
source_title: Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 summary
notes: Used for operational alignment; project does not claim legal compliance

claim: The European Supervisory Authorities designated critical ICT third-party providers in November 2025 using systemic importance, critical-function support and substitutability criteria
source_title: The European Supervisory Authorities designate critical ICT third-party providers under DORA
notes: Supports current supplier-concentration and supervisory context

claim: CISA described advanced threats to cloud identity involving token authentication, key management, logging, third-party dependencies and governance
source_title: Securing Core Cloud Identity Infrastructure
notes: Supports identity and token detection priorities

claim: MITRE ATT&CK v19 split the former Enterprise Defense Evasion tactic into Stealth and Defense Impairment
source_title: ATT&CK Updates - April 2026
notes: Current ATT&CK version at access date

claim: ICANN made RDAP the definitive source for gTLD registration data from 28 January 2025 in place of sunsetted WHOIS services
source_title: ICANN Update: Launching RDAP; Sunsetting WHOIS
notes: WHOIS may remain visible in tools but RDAP is the current standard for gTLD data

claim: FIRST states that TLP 2.0 is authoritative and uses RED, AMBER, GREEN and CLEAR
source_title: Traffic Light Protocol Version 2.0
notes: TLP:WHITE is deprecated

claim: FIRST EPSS estimates the probability of observing exploitation activity for a CVE during the next 30 days and EPSS v4 began publishing in March 2025
source_title: Exploit Prediction Scoring System
notes: EPSS does not include business impact or compensating controls

claim: STIX 2.1 and TAXII 2.1 are OASIS standards for representing and exchanging cyber-threat information
source_title: STIX 2.1 and TAXII 2.1
notes: TAXII is designed to exchange CTI including STIX content

claim: Sigma provides a generic detection-rule specification that can be converted to platform-specific query formats
source_title: Sigma Specification
notes: Production use still requires field mapping, tuning and testing

claim: MISP Workbench beta was released in 2026 as an analyst-focused workspace for combining intelligence from multiple sources
source_title: MISP Workbench v1.0 beta Released
notes: Supports shift from feed ingestion to analyst investigation

claim: The FBI warned that criminals use generative AI to improve phishing, translation, identity documents, audio and video impersonation for financial fraud
source_title: Criminals Use Generative Artificial Intelligence to Facilitate Financial Fraud
notes: Official warning supports process-verification controls; it does not quantify every AI-enabled loss

claim: Europol reported that caller ID spoofing supports large-scale cross-border financial fraud and undermines trust in displayed telephone numbers
source_title: Position Paper on Caller ID Spoofing
notes: Supports trusted-channel verification rather than reliance on displayed caller ID

claim: The FBI warned that malicious TDS infrastructure selectively redirects victims to financial phishing, scams or malware while showing safe content to non-targets and researchers
source_title: Cyber Criminals Redirecting Users to Fraudulent Websites with Malicious Traffic Distribution Systems
notes: Supports full redirect-chain analysis and preservation of victim context

claim: The FBI reported that Kali365 PhaaS uses device-code phishing to obtain Microsoft 365 access and refresh tokens and access Outlook, Teams and OneDrive without collecting the victim's password
source_title: Kali365 Phishing-as-a-Service Kit Hijacks Microsoft 365 Access Tokens
notes: First observed in April 2026; supports device-code and token-use detections

claim: Mandiant reported an UNC1069 intrusion against a cryptocurrency-sector fintech entity using a compromised Telegram account, fake Zoom meeting, ClickFix and reported AI-generated video
source_title: UNC1069 Targets Cryptocurrency Sector with New Tooling and AI-Enabled Social Engineering
notes: The source identified seven malware families and uses UNC1069 as a source-specific cluster label

claim: GTIG reported that UNC1069 compromised the axios maintainer account and introduced plain-crypto-js into axios versions 1.14.1 and 0.30.4 on 31 March 2026 to deploy WAVESHAPER.V2 across Windows, macOS and Linux
source_title: North Korea-Nexus Threat Actor Compromises Widely Used Axios NPM Package in Supply Chain Attack
notes: Demonstrates current developer and open-source supply-chain risk

claim: GTIG reported the first threat actor it assessed had used an AI-developed zero-day and broader use of AI for exploit development and adversarial workflows
source_title: Adversaries Leverage AI for Vulnerability Exploitation, Augmented Operations, and Initial Access
notes: Publisher assessment of AI assistance; does not mean every current exploit is AI-developed

claim: Mandiant stated that M-Trends 2026 data showed a mean time-to-exploit of negative seven days
source_title: Demystifying AI Exploits: A Blueprint for AI-Assisted Vulnerability Management
notes: Supports exposure reduction, pre-patch mitigations and retrospective hunting

claim: GTIG and Mandiant reported that most of the highest-impact supply-chain incidents they tracked during 2025 and early 2026 involved code repositories, dependencies and developer tools and assessed significant growth in large-scale open-source compromise
source_title: Batten Down Your Packages: Mitigation Guidance for Supply Chain Compromise
publisher: Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant
source_type: Primary threat research and mitigation guidance
notes: Elevates package-registry, repository and CI/CD telemetry; does not change the project's actor ranking

claim: GTIG introduced a unified cryptonym-based actor naming system and published mappings including UNC1069/MASAN to MIDNIGHT NEPTUNE, APT41 to SPIRE CASTLE and FIN11 to RAZOR COMET
source_title: Updated Cyber Threat Actor Naming System
notes: Mapping table appended 30 July 2026; historical source names remain preserved and cross-vendor equivalence is not assumed
